ev.q: Analysis of Early Hearing Detection and Intervention program survey data showed that, during 2006–2012
The proportion of infants identified with hearing loss increased from 1.1 to 1.6 per 1,000 infants screened
an average of 61.7% were documented as receiving EI in 2012 compared with 55.4% in 2006
The proportion of infants identified with hearing loss increased from 1.1 to 1.6 per 1,000 infants screened
an average of 96.6% of newborns were screened for hearing loss
The average percentage of LFU/LTD-DX decreased from 47.7% to 35.9%
The increase in documented cases was accompanied by a decrease in LFU/LTD-DX of 11.8% between 2006 and 2012

methods_quotes.q: Data for this report are based on the HSFS conducted for the years 2006–2012, using aggregate jurisdiction-reported totals.
Information was excluded if, after consultation with a jurisdictional EHDI program, the reported data were found to be incomplete or derived from estimated information.
The numbers of occurrent births are compared for accuracy with data from the jurisdiction's Vital Records program and the National Vital Statistics System.
The denominators for LFU/LTD-DX and LFU/LTD-EI used by CDC are total infants not passing the final hearing screening
